title: Halifax area Halifax Memorial
crew_summary: All killed (5 RCAF, 2 RAF); training flight in 10/10ths cloud
narrative: On the morning of 7 February 1944, Flight Lieutenant Hodson -- an experienced and decorated instructor pilot -- took his trainee crew up from Rufforth for a daytime training flight. The weather was appalling: total cloud covered the Yorkshire Wolds down to ground level. At 10:15 hours, flying blind, the Halifax struck the summit of Garrowby Hill at around 800 feet, one of the highest points on the A166 road between York and the coast. The aircraft crossed the road and exploded. At that precise moment, Arthur Kirkby was driving his milk collection lorry along the road on his rounds to the surrounding farms. The Halifax struck the lorry, killing Kirkby instantly alongside all seven airmen. Hodson, who held the Distinguished Flying Cross from operational service, was 30 years old -- the two youngest crew members, gunners McDonald and Booker, were both 19. One crew member initially survived the impact but died later in York Hospital. The regular bomb aimer, Alun Emlyn-Jones, had been taken off the flight that morning due to an erupting appendix -- a twist of fate that saved his life and drove him, decades later, to campaign for a permanent memorial.

crew.name: Alfred John Shirley Hodson DFC
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Halifax DK192 struck the summit of Garrowby Hill in total cloud cover. Hodson was an experienced instructor pilot who held the Distinguished Flying Cross from operational service.
crew.bio: An experienced and decorated instructor pilot, Hodson held the DFC from operational service. At 30, he was the eldest of the crew.

cause_of_loss: Flew into hilltop in 10/10ths cloud; struck road and milk lorry
memorial_details:
Name: Handley Page Halifax DK192
Type: Stone of remembrance
Description: Large upright stone of remembrance. Made of grey granite. Incised lettering.
Inscription: AT THIS PLACE ON/ 7TH FEBRUARY 1944 AT 10AM/ HALIFAX BOMBER DK 192/ FROM RAF RUFFORTH, CRASHED IN/ 10/10THS CLOUD DURING A TRAINING FLIGHT./ ALL ON BOARD AND THE DRIVER OF/ A MILK LORRY WHO WAS PASSING/ ALONG THIS ROAD WERE KILLED./ [crew names inscribed on memorial]/ ERECTED BY THEIR COMRADE/ (Name)/ WE WILL REMEMBER THEM.
Location: On the GARROWBY HILL Off A166 Youlthorpe East Yorkshire Antrim England
Grid Ref: SE 760 550
Coordinates: 53.985473556980,-0.842459147788
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/18/384/large_35102_copyright_stephen_lowe.jpg

The Handley Page Halifax DK192 memorial is a stone of remembrance located on Garrowby Hill off A166 in Youlthorpe, East Yorkshire.

The memorial was unveiled in May 1996.

The Crew of Halifax Bomber DK 192 Memorial is a stone of remembrance located in the hedge of a layby on the A166, 150 metres east of Cat Nab Farm near Garrowby Hill.

Unveiling Ceremony (May 1996): The unveiling of the Handley Page Halifax DK192 stone of remembrance.

Memorial Unveiling: The memorial was paid for by the Bomb Aimer who survived the tragedy.

Memorial Stone Unveiling (8th May 1996): A memorial stone was erected at the crash site and unveiled.

external_narratives.summary: Page for Fl/Lt Alfred John Shirley Hodson DFC and crew of Halifax DK192, 1663 HCU RAF Rufforth. On 7 February 1944, the aircraft flew into the summit of Garrowby Hill in total cloud cover, also killing civilian milk lorry driver Arthur Kirkby.
external_narratives.key_details: Hodson held the DFC from operational service and was aged 30. Regular bomb aimer Alun Emlyn-Jones was removed from the flight due to an erupting appendix, saving his life. He later campaigned for the memorial. One crew member initially survived but died in York Hospital.
external_narratives.link_description: Poignant tribute to Fl/Lt Alfred John Shirley Hodson and crew's Halifax DK192 tragedy at Rufforth.

external_narratives.summary: Imperial War Museum register entry for the Halifax DK192 memorial on Garrowby Hill. Granite memorial stone erected through the efforts of Alun Emlyn-Jones, the surviving crew member.
external_narratives.key_details: Memorial reference 35102. Dedicated 8 May 1996. Located in a lay-by on the A166, Garrowby Hill, approximately 6 miles east of Stamford Bridge.

external_narratives.key_details: Crash at 10:15 hours. Aircraft crossed the road and caught fire. Milk lorry driver Arthur Wood Kirkby killed. Unit was 1663 HCU, not 1663 as sometimes misquoted.
